artworks.title: Medea about to Kill her Children
artworks.description: Delacroix's Louvre Medea — the Colchian pressed into a cave with her children and a dagger, Euripides' Corinthian revenge at the brink of the act.

artworks.title: Medea
artworks.description: Feuerbach's seated sorceress holds the fatal gifts — cool neoclassical calm before the bridal fire and the children's deaths.

artworks.title: Medea's Gift to Creusa (Louvre CA 2193)
artworks.description: Apulian crater: Creusa receives Medea's bridal gifts while the children stand by — the poisoned robe and diadem frozen in clay.

artworks.title: Medea, or the Marriage of Jason and Creusa
artworks.description: Rembrandt's etching for Jan Six's Medea — Jason and Creusa at the altar while the Colchian's tragedy gathers offstage.

artworks.title: Medea Sarcophagus (Berlin)
artworks.description: Roman sarcophagus: the children carry poisoned wedding gifts to Creusa — Corinth's crimes carved beside the infanticide.

popCulture.title: Medea (play)
popCulture.creator: Euripides
popCulture.description: Euripides' Corinth — Jason's betrayal and Medea's revenge — remains the West's most staged portrait of a wronged sorceress.

popCulture.title: Medea
popCulture.description: The Colchian who kills her children to wound Jason — Corinth fixes her forever as tragedy's most terrible mother.
